title: Check Engine Light Diagnosis
subtitle: We'll read the code, judge urgency, try safe DIY fixes when they fit, and know when to stop and see a pro — you've got a coach in the passenger seat.
tone: Calm diagnostic coach. Never scare, never dismiss. Flashing CEL = immediate action. Prefer OBD photo/video guidance over jargon walls.
prerequisites: OBD-II scanner or Bluetooth adapter + phone app (1996+ US vehicles)
Note: flashing light + rough running = reduce load / stop safe ASAP
Recent fuel quality / fill-up notes help
tools_checklist: Optional: gas cap, MAF cleaner, gloves
parts_checklist: Depends on code — common: gas cap, air filter, spark plugs/coils, O2 sensor, thermostat
Do not buy parts until codes + symptoms point clearly

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Flashing Check Engine while driving usually means active misfire — catalytic converter risk. Ease off, stop safe, don't ignore.
Many solid CELs after fueling are EVAP / loose gas cap. Easy DIY check first — but confirm with the actual code.
Hybrids can set ICE and hybrid-system codes. A basic $20 code reader may miss manufacturer-specific hybrid modules — shop-level scan if the light returns with ready/HV warnings.
Diesel CELs often involve emissions (DPF, DEF, EGR). Forcing 'just clear the code' can leave you in limp mode — diagnose properly.
European cars store codes across many modules. Generic OBD may only show P0xxx — a shop scan is worth it if symptoms persist.
Higher-mile engines with misfire codes often need plugs/coils/vacuum inspection — still verify the code before spraying parts at it.

steps.title: Check Engine is on — we'll sort it calmly
steps.description: First question: is the light solid or flashing? Is the car driving normally, rough, or losing power? Answer that and we'll pick a safe path.
steps.safety_warning: Flashing CEL + shaking/rough running: reduce speed, avoid highway hills, stop somewhere safe. Continuing can destroy the catalytic converter.

steps.title: Flashing light — protect the cat
steps.description: Treat this like an active misfire until proven otherwise. Stop hard acceleration. If safe, park and arrange a scan today. Towing beats a $1k+ converter.
steps.safety_warning: Do not clear codes and keep driving on a flashing light — that hides the warning without fixing the misfire.

action_buttons.label: Describe symptoms in chat
action_buttons.payload: CEL is flashing. Symptoms: (noise, rpm shake, power loss). What should I do right now?

steps.title: Plug in and read the code(s)
steps.description: OBD port is usually under the dash left of the steering column. Key on (engine may stay off). Record every code and freeze-frame if shown — photos help.
steps.safety_warning: Park in park/neutral with brake on. Don't leave adapters dangling where feet kick them while driving.

steps.title: Plain-English meaning
steps.description: Share the code with me in chat (e.g. P0302, P0420, P0457). I'll translate causes by likelihood for your mileage and engine — we won't shotgun parts.

variants.description: High-mile context: misfires and catalyst efficiency codes show up more — still confirm with the scanner before buying coils or a catalytic converter.
If you also see Ready / HV warnings, say so — those need a hybrid-capable scan, not only a generic P-code app.

steps.title: DIY: gas cap & easy EVAP checks
steps.description: Inspect the cap seal, tighten until it clicks, check for a cracked hose only if you're comfortable under the hood visually. Clear codes only after the fix — then drive a few cycles to confirm.
steps.safety_warning: Don't clear codes to pass inspection without a fix — they often return, and you lose freeze-frame clues.

steps.title: Safe DIY vs shop diagnostics
steps.description: DIY-friendly: gas cap, air filter, careful MAF clean (right cleaner only), plug/coil swap when codes name a cylinder. Shop-level: catalyst, timing, wiring, fuel trim mysteries, diesel emissions, hybrid modules.
steps.safety_warning: If performance is poor, temp climbs, or oil/coolant mixes — stop DIY and get help.

variants.description: If a generic reader only shows one vague code, pay for a full-system scan before ordering OEM sensors.

steps.title: Optional DIY: careful MAF clean
steps.description: Only if codes/symptoms fit (hesitation, fuel trims, MAF codes). Engine off. Disconnect sensor. Spray MAF cleaner only — never carb cleaner, never touch the wire. Air dry fully before install.
steps.safety_warning: Wrong cleaner destroys the sensor. If you're unsure it's the MAF, skip this and chat with the code first.

steps.title: Monitor drive cycles & log it
steps.description: Write down codes, what you tried, and mileage. Note if the light returns. Ready for inspection monitors may need several drive cycles after a clear.

completion.description: Keep the code list in your health file. If it returns with new symptoms, don't clear repeatedly — bring freeze-frame data to a tech.
